TOKENS ARE NOT RECONSTRUCTED BY THE BRIDGE. This board was lifted with four of our creatures and the log shows eight: Mogg War Marshal and three Goblin Tokens (ids 371, 1706, 1707, 1708) were added by hand from the log, which names every one of them as a target of a Brute Force copy. Without them the board contradicted the stack — the resolver flagged exactly this.

THE CUT HAS AN EMPTY STACK ON PURPOSE. An earlier draft of this file carried the Brute Force cast in BOTH `stack` and `actions`, which made the board say seat-3 holds priority while our spell was already on the stack. v2 resolves `actions` left to right, so the cast lives there alone. The checker caught this; it was an authoring error, not the resolver's.
extras.provenance: Lifted from a real Forge game, not authored: run …n60-…-meExperimental-podExperimental-c600, game 17, global turn 40, replay `-n 2 -s 1383481154`. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE LIFT, both recorded rather than hidden: (1) the bridge does not reconstruct tokens, so four of our eight creatures were missing and were added from the log; (2) the cut is at precombat main, but the log shows the cast occurring LATER in the same turn, during jarad-graveyard's combat after blockers were declared (our eight creatures were blocking Jarad and Splinterfright). The scenario poses the same spell on the same board at an earlier priority window because the question — how many copies, are they cast, resulting P/T — is unaffected by the step. Nothing here claims a combat outcome. This board is the zada-v1 BRANCH: the sleeved 99 runs neither Brute Force nor Firebrand Archer.

scenario.question: During jarad-graveyard's precombat main phase we cast Brute Force (instant, "Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn") targeting ONLY Zada, Hedron Grinder, with seven other creatures on our battlefield. (a) How many copies does Zada's triggered ability create and what does each one target? (b) Are those copies CAST, and what follows from the answer? (c) What is each of our creatures' power and toughness once the original and every copy has resolved?

steps.action: We cast Brute Force (instant, {R}, "Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn") during seat-3 (jarad-graveyard)'s precombat main phase, choosing Zada, Hedron Grinder as its one and only target. We are not the active player.
steps.effect: Legal: Brute Force is an instant, so it may be cast in another player's main phase any time we hold priority. Its single target is locked in as the spell goes on the stack and cannot be changed later. Zada is the ONLY target of the spell, which is the precondition Zada's ability names. THE CUT'S STACK IS EMPTY (`scenario.stack` is `[]`) and the cast lives in `actions` alone, so our Brute Force is the first object to go on the stack and sits at the bottom of it. HOW priority reached us is not reconstructed by the bridge and is not argued here: the cast is OBSERVED (`actions[0].observed_in_log` is true, and the log line is quoted below), and a player may cast an instant only when they have priority, so 117.1a is satisfied by observation. Round 2 carried a priority-reconstruction step ahead of this one; round 3 DROPPED it as ungrounded rather than repair it (see revision_notes). Provenance: the log line is `Add To Stack: Ai(4)-mm-goblin-storm-zada-v1 cast Brute Force targeting [Zada, Hedron Grinder (403)]`; this is an observed cast, not a prediction. Card membership (scenario-facts): Brute Force and Firebrand Archer are in the zada-v1 BRANCH list only -- `card_membership.NOT_IN_THE_DECK` names Firebrand Archer and the sleeved goblin-storm 99 contains neither card -- so this line is one the branch can run and the current sleeved deck cannot.

steps.action: Two of our triggered abilities match the cast event: Zada, Hedron Grinder ("Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada, copy that spell for each other creature you control that the spell could target. Each copy targets a different one of those creatures.") and Firebrand Archer ("Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, this creature deals 1 damage to each opponent.").
steps.effect: ONE cast event occurred, so each ability triggers exactly ONCE. Both trigger conditions are satisfied by that single cast: Brute Force targets only Zada, and Brute Force is a noncreature spell. The log agrees and shows exactly one of each (`triggered Firebrand Archer`, `triggered Zada, Hedron Grinder`). Round 1 declared the ORDERING of the two out of scope; round 2 settles it in step 3, because a resolution cannot narrate an unwind without committing to one.

citations.quote: Any abilities that trigger when a spell is cast or put onto the stack trigger at this time
Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers

steps.action: Both triggered abilities go on the stack above Brute Force before any player next receives priority. Multiple abilities triggered since the last time a player received priority and we control both, so the two-part 603.3b process applies and, within our own APNAP slot, WE choose the order. We choose: Firebrand Archer's trigger on first, Zada's trigger on top of it.
steps.effect: Resulting stack, bottom-up: Brute Force (pos 0), Firebrand Archer's trigger (pos 1), Zada's trigger (pos 2, topmost). Each object put on the stack goes on top of everything already there, so both abilities resolve before the spell that triggered them -- which is what Firebrand Archer's official 2017-07-14 ruling describes ("Firebrand Archer's ability will resolve before the spell that caused it to trigger"); the CR rules cited here are what make it so, and the ruling holds under EITHER ordering, since the original Brute Force resolves last in both. THE ORDERING MATTERS TO THE NARRATION AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG. Under the ordering taken here, Zada's trigger resolves first and the seven copies it creates go on top of everything already on the stack -- the Archer trigger INCLUDED -- so the Archer trigger is buried beneath all seven and resolves after them (step 7). Under the other ordering (Zada's trigger first, Archer's on top) the Archer trigger resolves FIRST, before Zada's ability and before any copy exists. What no ordering permits is the sequence round 1 narrated: the Archer trigger resolving after Zada's ability but before the copies. 405.2 forbids it, and round 1 cited 405.2 itself. Nothing in (a), (b) or (c) depends on which of the two legal orderings we take: Firebrand Archer deals 1 damage to each opponent either way, and its own power is not involved in its ability.

steps.action: (a) Zada's triggered ability, topmost, resolves. It copies Brute Force once for each OTHER creature we control that Brute Force could target, each copy targeting a different one of those creatures.
steps.effect: SEVEN copies, one each for the seven other creatures we control, each targeting a different one: the three 1/1 red Goblin tokens (log ids 1706, 1707, 1708), Siege-Gang Commander, Mogg War Marshal (log id 371), Broadside Bombardiers and Firebrand Archer. Zada itself is excluded by the word "other" and receives only the ORIGINAL spell. Every one of the seven is a creature we control and none has shroud, protection or any other targeting restriction in its oracle text, so under 707.10d no copy is withheld. The copies are put on the stack in the order of our choice, on top of everything already there -- which now includes the Archer trigger from step 3 as well as the original. PROVENANCE OF THE BOARD (round 1 reported a data discrepancy here; it has been resolved and the claim is withdrawn): the bridge does not reconstruct tokens, and the lift originally carried only four of our eight bodies, so Mogg War Marshal and the three Goblin tokens were added to the scenario by hand from the log, which names every one of them as the target of a Brute Force copy. `extras.reconstruction_notes` and `extras.provenance` record that correction rather than hiding it. As the scenario now stands, `scenario.seats['you'].board` and `scenario-facts.your_board.creature_bodies` report the SAME eight bodies, with no duplicate and nothing invented, so there is no disagreement between the data sources and this artifact asserts none.

steps.action: (b) Are the copies CAST? No. A copy created by a resolving ability is PUT onto the stack; it is not cast.
steps.effect: The log prints `cast Brute Force targeting [Goblin Token (1708)]` for each copy. That wording is Forge's internal log vocabulary, NOT a rules claim, and the rules are explicit the other way: to copy a spell means to put a copy onto the stack, and a copy of a spell isn't cast. Casting is a specific action -- taking a card from the zone it is in, putting it on the stack and paying its costs -- and none of that happens for these seven copies (nor is {R} paid seven more times; `mana.open` is 1, which `extras.reconstruction_notes` defines as the untapped-land count, so that is an illustration and not the ground of the conclusion, which rests on 707.10 alone). WHAT FOLLOWS, and this board is where it is observable: (i) Firebrand Archer, which triggers on a noncreature spell being CAST, triggers ONCE for the original and NOT for any of the seven copies -- eight Archer triggers would be the wrong reading, and the log shows one; (ii) Zada's own ability, which also triggers on a cast, does NOT re-trigger off its own copies, so there is no loop and no storm out of this line; (iii) the copies are still spells for every other purpose -- they resolve, they can be countered, and they target legally -- so each does apply its +3/+3.

steps.action: Priority is passed and the stack unwinds last-in-first-out. The seven copies are the top seven objects, so they resolve one at a time, each granting its own target +3/+3 until end of turn.
steps.effect: Each resolution is followed by the active player (seat-3) receiving priority and by the usual priority round, and the stack resolves top-down, so all seven copies resolve before anything beneath them. Each resolved +3/+3 is a continuous effect lasting until end of turn, applied in layer 7c as a modification of power and toughness -- it does not set them, so it stacks additively on the creature's printed values. Exactly one instance applies to each of our seven other creatures.

steps.effect: One trigger, one instance of its effect: 1 damage PER OPPONENT SEAT. The opponent count is taken from the LIVE SEAT LIST -- `scenario.seats` carries seat-2, seat-3 and seat-4 besides us, and `scenario-facts.drain_arithmetic.opponents` is 3 -- so that is 1 per seat and 3 across the pod. The two figures are not interchangeable and the pod total is never quoted as a per-seat number. WHY 704.5a IS CITED HERE: the bridge records seat-2 at 0 life and seat-4 at -5 life (`drain_arithmetic.per_opponent_life` = [0, 21, -5]) while both still control permanents. A player at 0 or less life loses the game as a state-based action, so in a live game both would already have left and the pod total for this trigger would be 1, not 3. Those life figures are therefore stale last-observed bridge output, not a legal game state, which is why the 3-opponent count above comes from the seat list and not from life. Round 1 asserted that no claim in the artifact depended on those life totals; that was wrong -- the pod figure did -- and the dependency is now stated instead of denied. No kill is computed here and none is claimed.

steps.action: (c) Read the resulting power and toughness off each creature's printed values plus its one +3/+3, then total the eight bodies.
steps.effect: Per creature: Zada, Hedron Grinder 3/3 -> 6/6 (the original only); Firebrand Archer 2/1 -> 5/4; Broadside Bombardiers 2/2 -> 5/5; Siege-Gang Commander 2/2 -> 5/5; Mogg War Marshal 1/1 -> 4/4; each of the three 1/1 red Goblin tokens -> 4/4. TOTALS, CORRECTED: BEFORE is 13 power and 12 toughness (power 3+2+2+2+1+1+1+1 = 13; toughness 3+1+2+2+1+1+1+1 = 12). AFTER is 37 power and 36 toughness -- +3/+3 on each of eight bodies is +24/+24, so 13+24 = 37 and 12+24 = 36, and the after-values sum to the same thing directly (6+5+5+5+4+4+4+4 = 37 power; 6+4+5+5+4+4+4+4 = 36 toughness). ROUND 1 PUBLISHED 14/15 -> 33/33 AND ALL FOUR FIGURES WERE WRONG while every per-creature value above them was right: 33 is the sum of only SEVEN of the eight after-values, inside a total that simultaneously claimed eight bodies. The headline in `final_state.summary` carried the same two wrong numbers and is corrected with them. Base values are the printed P/T from the branch `cards.json` and the scenario's own `pt` fields, which agree; our board carries no anthem, no counters and no other permanents at all (`scenario-facts.your_board.other_permanents` is empty), so printed = current. The three tokens are 1/1 red Goblins created by SIEGE-GANG COMMANDER's enters-the-battlefield trigger. That is ESTABLISHED, not uncertain, and round 2's hedge is withdrawn: LOG LINE 2551 reads "When Siege-Gang Commander enters, create three 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens", and ids 1706/1707/1708 are those three -- three consecutive ids from one simultaneous three-token creation, which Mogg War Marshal ("create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token", one at a time) cannot produce. The scenario's board annotations now record exactly this. Their 1/1 is therefore the P/T the creating ability's own wording specifies, and it matches the board's `pt` fields.

steps.effect: Nothing of ours leaves the battlefield from this line: every one of our eight creatures ends with toughness 4 or greater, so none has toughness 0 or less and none is put into a graveyard. Brute Force only adds to toughness, so no toughness check can newly fail during the unwind either, and no damage is marked on our creatures at this priority window. Lethal damage (704.5g) is therefore not reached. The one other state-based action this board implicates, 704.5a on the two recorded life totals, is handled at step 7 rather than here, because it bears on the Archer trigger's pod figure and not on our bodies.

final_state.summary: One {R} instant targeting only Zada becomes eight instances of +3/+3. (a) Zada's ability creates SEVEN copies of Brute Force, one for each other creature we control that the spell could target, each targeting a different one -- three 1/1 Goblin tokens, Siege-Gang Commander, Mogg War Marshal, Broadside Bombardiers, Firebrand Archer -- put on the stack above everything already there in our chosen order. (b) The copies are NOT cast: to copy a spell is to PUT a copy onto the stack, and the log's word "cast" is Forge's vocabulary, not the CR's. That is observable here: Firebrand Archer triggers ONCE, on the original, not eight times, and Zada does not re-trigger off her own copies, so there is no loop. (c) Zada 6/6; Firebrand Archer 5/4; Broadside Bombardiers 5/5; Siege-Gang Commander 5/5; Mogg War Marshal 4/4; each of three Goblin tokens 4/4 -- 37 power and 36 toughness across eight bodies, up from 13/12. Nothing of ours dies. We control both triggers, so we order them: Firebrand Archer's under Zada's, which puts the Archer trigger beneath the seven copies and resolves it after them and before the original. This is the zada-v1 BRANCH board: the sleeved goblin-storm 99 runs neither Brute Force nor Firebrand Archer.

final_state.scope: Deliberately limited to ONE rules domain: copying a spell. Trigger ORDERING is no longer deferred -- step 3 commits to a legal ordering under 603.3b and states what the alternative would change -- but combat, blocks and any lethal arithmetic are NOT resolved here and no claim above depends on them.
revision_notes: Round 2, finding 1 (now step 9): the totals were wrong and the error was in the headline. Corrected to 13/12 before and 37/36 after, in the step, in final_state.totals and in final_state.summary; the per-creature values, which the checker upheld, are unchanged.

Round 2, finding 2 (now step 4): the DATA DISCREPANCY paragraph is withdrawn. The board was corrected between rounds by adding Mogg War Marshal and three Goblin tokens from the log, and scenario-facts and the board now both report eight bodies. Rewritten as a provenance note.

Round 2, finding 3 (now split across steps 3, 6, 7 and 8): the Archer trigger's resolution was placed where no ordering permits. Step 3 applies 603.3b, commits to Archer-under-Zada, and states that the copies go on top of the Archer trigger under 405.2; the Archer trigger accordingly resolves at step 7, after all seven copies and before the original at step 8.

Round 2, finding 4: two of the three added citations stand -- 603.3b at step 3 (how two triggers from one event reach the stack) and 704.5a at step 7 (the recorded 0 and -5 life totals are stale bridge output, and the 3-opponent count comes from the seat list, not from life). The third pair, 117.3a/117.3d on a round-2 priority step, is GONE: see the next note.

ROUND 3, CHANGE 1 -- THE PRIORITY STEP IS DROPPED, not argued. Round 2's step 1 and both of its citations (117.3a, 117.3d) are removed and every later step renumbered (old 2-11 -> new 1-10). The step's claim was wrong, not merely thin: turn order across the scenario's own seat list runs seat-2 (sythis), seat-3 (jarad, ACTIVE), seat-4 (abaddon), you, so the next player after the active seat-3 is SEAT-4, not us, and the step narrated a one-pass hand-off from seat-3 straight to us. Nothing in (a), (b) or (c) ever depended on how priority reached us: we hold it and we cast, which `actions` states and the log observes. Dropped as ungrounded rather than patched with a second pass.

ROUND 3, CHANGE 2 -- the token attribution no longer hedges. Step 9 and gaps[0] stated that the artifact 'does NOT attribute the three tokens to one maker' while the scenario's board annotations attributed them definitively; the checker called that self-contradiction, and the annotations are right. Both now state it as ESTABLISHED and cite log line 2551 ("When Siege-Gang Commander enters, create three 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens"), with ids 1706/1707/1708 as those three. No figure moves -- a 1/1 red Goblin is a 1/1 red Goblin -- so this is a consistency fix, not an arithmetic one.

ROUND 3, CHANGE 3 -- `scenario.stack` is EMPTY at the cut and the Brute Force cast lives in `actions` alone (an earlier draft of the scenario wrongly carried it in both, which is what made the round-2 priority narration look necessary). Step 1 now states the empty cut-stack and that our Brute Force is therefore the bottom object. No surviving step argued from a non-empty stack, so nothing else needed rewording.

Citation count 30 -> 28, back inside the <=32 band; no fourth question is answered. AFTER RENUMBERING, every one of the 28 (step, rule) pairs was re-checked against the claim the round-2 checker verified it on, and all 28 sit on the same claims at their new numbers.

Their origin is ESTABLISHED -- log line 2551 reads "When Siege-Gang Commander enters, create three 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens" and ids 1706/1707/1708 are those three, which the scenario's board annotations state -- so the round-2 'maker not attributed' disclaimer is withdrawn as an incomplete retraction rather than left contradicting the board. seat-2 is recorded at 0 life and seat-4 at -5. Under 704.5a neither is a legal game state, so they are stale last-observed bridge output. Step 7 states the one place this bears on a figure: Firebrand Archer's POD total would be 1 rather than 3 if those totals held. The PER-SEAT figure (1 damage per opponent) is unaffected, and no player-loss or kill claim is made.

Brute Force has NO official WotC rulings (scenario-facts rulings.cards), and neither does Mogg War Marshal. Zada, Hedron Grinder and Firebrand Archer both have rulings and both agree with the resolution above -- Zada's 2018-03-16 rulings state the copies "are created on the stack, so they're not cast", that shroud/protection creatures are "just ignored", and that the original "will resolve last"; Firebrand Archer's 2017-07-14 ruling states its ability resolves before the spell that triggered it, which holds under either trigger ordering. Rulings are inputs only; every citation above is a CR rule or a glossary term.

The scenario's own provenance records that the logged cast happened later in seat-3's turn, during combat after blockers were declared, rather than at the precombat main the cut names. Nothing in (a), (b) or (c) depends on the phase or the step, and round 3 dropped the round-2 step that reconstructed how priority reached us, so no claim here turns on the window at all: the cast is observed, and casting an instant requires priority.

THE ONE DEFECT THAT REMAINS, and it is not a renumbering defect. The quote is exact ('If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.') and 704.5a does establish that the board as posed is not a legal game state. What it CANNOT establish is the step's next inference, which is the claim it is attached to: 'Those life figures are therefore stale last-observed bridge output, not a legal game state, which is why the 3-opponent count above comes from the seat list and not from life.' The step picks which half of a self-contradictory board to discard, and THE LOG DECIDES IT THE OTHER WAY. In the source game (part-01.log, game bounded 1427-2712, the cut at turn 40 = line 2556): seat-2 sythis reached 0 life at line 2227 and seat-4 abaddon reached -5 at line 2512, BOTH BEFORE THE CUT, and the values match the recorded 0 and -5 exactly -- so the life totals are accurate, not stale. The dispositive evidence is the Archer trigger itself. An earlier Archer trigger with all three opponents alive printed THREE damage lines and THREE life lines (1836-1841). The trigger at this cut printed ONE: 'Damage: Firebrand Archer (396) deals 1 non-combat damage to Ai(2)-mm-jarad-graveyard' / 'Life: Ai(2)-mm-jarad-graveyard 21 > 20' (2578-2579). Exactly one opponent was in the game. So the pod total for this trigger is 1, the SEAT LIST is the stale half, and the step's 'so that is 1 per seat and 3 across the pod' is contradicted by the board it was lifted from. HOW MUCH IT MATTERS: not at all to (a), (b) or (c); no kill is computed and the per-seat figure is unaffected. But it is a statement of fact in the wrong direction on the exact per-seat/pod axis the charter flags, the resolver named the dependency and then resolved it against evidence in the file it was already quoting for step 9, and it propagates to final_state.gaps[1] (same inversion) and to final_state.opponents[], which publishes change_from_this_line -1 for two seats that were already out. The fix is a clause, not a rewrite: state that the log shows two seats had already lost before the cut, that the pod total here is 1, and that the three-seat list is the bridge's stale record (800.4a is the rule for a player leaving a multiplayer game); keep 704.5a, which is the right rule for the observation.
